title: Constraints on the electron-to-proton mass ratio variation at the epoch of reionization
question: Constrain variation of the electron-to-proton mass ratio mu at z > 6 from velocity offsets between [CI]/[CII] fine-structure lines and CO rotational lines in two quasar hosts, and combine with all other Delta mu/mu estimates to test a redshift dependence

data.angular_resolution: J0439+1634 IRAM/NOEMA detections are spatially unresolved despite differing beams

what.value: IRAM/NOEMA spectra and line parameters of J0439+1634 (Table 1 is the authors' Gaussian refit of these spectra)

evidence.quote: using published IRAM/NOEMA spectra of the most distant gravitationally lensed quasar J0439+1634

what.value: Redshifts, FWHM and channel widths of CO and [CII] lines of J2310+1855 (Table 2 of L20)

evidence.quote: The detected molecular lines are listed in Table 2 of L20.

what.value: Delta mu/mu = (-1.3 +/- 7.9)e-5 at z = 6.419 towards J1148+5251, combined into the weighted mean

evidence.quote: another high redshift value of $\Delta\mu/\mu$ = $(-1.3\pm7.9)\times10^{-5}$ at $z = 6.419$ towards the quasar J1148+5251 (Levshakov et al. 2017)

what.value: Electron mass at recombination m_e,z = (1.0190 +/- 0.0055) m_e,0 used as the z=1100 point of the regression

evidence.quote: Exploiting the value of $m_{{\rm e},z} = (1.0190\pm0.0055)m_{\rm e,0}$ at $z = 1100$ from Hart & Chluba (2020)

what.value: Compilation of Delta mu/mu measurements from z=0 to z=5.24 (Milky Way, LMC, M33, PKS 1413+135, B0218+357, J0134-0931, PKS1830-211, H2 systems, RXJ0911.4+0551, HLSJ091828.6+514223) used in the regression

evidence.quote: The data points shown in Fig. [3](#Fg3) were compiled from the following sources.

external_data.citation: Levshakov et al. 2013, 2012, 2017, 2019; Kanekar et al. 2010, 2011, 2012, 2015, 2018; Daprà et al. 2017; Ubachs et al. 2016, 2019; Weiß et al. 2012

what.value: Laboratory rest frequencies of CO, [CI] and [CII]

external_data.citation: Endres et al. 2016; Haris & Kramida 2017; Cooksy et al. 1986

recipe.method: Baselines fitted by regression to line-free spectral intervals and subtracted; mean rms assigned to whole spectrum
assumptions: Individual rms uncertainties of the same order, so their mean is used for the whole spectrum

recipe.method: Single-component Gaussian fit to each of [CII], [CI], CO(6-5), CO(7-6), CO(9-8); CO(10-9) excluded because blended
assumptions: Alpha is kept fixed, so Delta F/F = -Delta mu/mu

recipe.goal: Delta mu/mu from J0439+1634 at z=6.519
recipe.method: Average redshifts separately of fine-structure lines and of CO lines, then Delta mu/mu = (<z>_rot - <z>_fs)/(1 + zbar)
assumptions: Doppler noise is normally distributed with zero mean and finite variance, so averaging over lines gives the signal

recipe.goal: Delta mu/mu from J2310+1855 at z=6.003
recipe.method: Average five CO redshifts from L20 and compare with [CII] redshift
assumptions: [CII] and CO lines co-spatially distributed (similar widths)

recipe.method: Weighted mean of Delta mu/mu at z=6.519, 6.003 and 6.419 (J1148+5251)

recipe.goal: Fit redshift dependence of Delta mu/mu
recipe.method: Regression of power law Delta mu/mu = k_mu (1+z)^p to all compiled points from z=0 to z=1100; exponential alternative also tried
assumptions: Electron mass shift at recombination from Hart & Chluba (2020) is real

evidence.quote: we set a limit on $\Delta\mu/\mu$ $= (0.0 \pm 2.7)\times10^{-5}$ at $z = 6.519$.

answer_key.quantity: Weighted mean Delta mu/mu at zbar=6.3 (three quasars)

evidence.quote: give a mean value of $\langle \Delta\mu/\mu \rangle = (0.7 \pm 1.2)\times 10^{-5}$ at $\bar{z} = 6.3$

answer_key.quantity: Mean redshift of fine-structure lines of J0439+1634

evidence.quote: It gives $\langle z \rangle_{\rm fs} = 6.51885(18)$ and $\langle z \rangle_{\rm rot} = 6.51885(9)$.

answer_key.quantity: Mean redshift of CO lines of J0439+1634

evidence.quote: It gives $\langle z \rangle_{\rm fs} = 6.51885(18)$ and $\langle z \rangle_{\rm rot} = 6.51885(9)$.

answer_key.quantity: CO(7-6) velocity offset from [CII] in J0439+1634

evidence.quote: with the velocity offset $\Delta V = 20.3$ km s$^{-1}$

not_stated_but_needed: How the weighted mean and its error are computed for combining redshifts and for the final z=6.3 mean (formula, treatment of Doppler noise term)
How the uncertainty on <z>_fs and <z>_rot and on Delta mu/mu is propagated
Which individual line redshifts for J0439+1634 are averaged (Table 1 values) and the exact data points and weights, including any systematic terms, entering the regression for k_mu and p
The regression method (weighted least squares, priors, software) and how the z=1100 point is converted to Delta mu/mu
Baseline polynomial order and the line-free intervals used for the spectra
Which L20 CO lines (and which sources of redshifts) make up the five averaged for J2310+1855 and why CO(5-4) NOEMA and CO(6-5) ALMA/NOEMA are both listed
Calibration, imaging and reduction of the ALMA data (done in L20, not here)
missing_for_reproduction: Exact formulas and weights for the weighted means and the regression
Tabulated line redshifts for J0439+1634 are in Table 1 but flux-density spectra must be taken from Y19
Compiled Delta mu/mu points for all redshifts are given only in the Appendix text, not a machine-readable table
score_reason: Inputs are published tables and a few simple averages and a two-parameter regression, but the weighting and regression details are not given.
rediscovery_reason: Data are public via cited papers, recipe is short (average redshifts, difference, weighted mean, fit), and all main results are numeric; weighting conventions must be inferred.
